articles.title: At least 13 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications

At least 13 people have died, and more than 300 have been hospitalised since November 18 after they consumed spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district, police said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The patients are mostly from Chakpikarong and surrounding areas and have been hospitalised across multiple healthcare facilities in Imphal, including JNIMS, RIMS, Shija and Babina Hospital.

"Thirteen people have been reported dead till 9 p.m. on Friday, while 346 patients have been admitted to hospitals due to suspected methanol poisoning, as they consumed spurious liquor," an official told PTI .
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited Shija Hospital and Babina Hospital on Friday afternoon (November 20, 2026) to assess the situation and meet patients undergoing treatment.

In a social media post, Mr. Singh said, "Visited Shija Hospital at Lamphelpat, and Babina Hospital at Sajiwa, today [on Friday] to enquire about the health condition of the persons undergoing treatment after consuming spurious liquor from Chakpikarong area in Chandel District."
The Chandel district administration has intensified emergency response measures, and a team has been constituted for coordinated monitoring of the situation, an official notification said.
Four rapid response teams, equipped with adequate medicines and oxygen supplies, have been deployed in the district, the official said.

"Over 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The death toll has touched 11 during the last 48 hours. The patients are undergoing medical evaluation and treatment under the close supervision of the doctors," he said.

"A medical team, led by a Specialist in General Medicine, along with essential medicines, has left for Chandel District to strengthen on-ground treatment and response", he said adding, "The government will conduct an enquiry and the culprits will be punished."
Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan .K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will; the demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA rigging; this fight isn’t over,’ said a protester

Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.

The peaceful sit-in was forcibly broken up by police on Saturday night (November 21), said the protesters. “Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will. The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.
Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”
The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.
On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.

articles.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.
In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka.
He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner.

Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added.

articles.title: Municipal staff transfers to move online by Tamil Nadu govt., with vacancies displayed on portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be eligible for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

The Tamil Nadu government has introduced online counselling for transfers and postings of employees in municipal corporations, municipal councils and town panchayats, covering employees in the lower and middle levels of the government pay structure, including posts such as assistants, junior assistants and superintendents. The guidelines were issued through two Government Orders (G.O.s) by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department dated November 19, 2026.
The counselling will be based on vacancies and station seniority. The online portal is being developed by the respective heads of departments and will be introduced shortly, an official said.

Regarding whether employees would be able to raise grievances relating to seniority or other issues through the portal, the official said the department would be asked to incorporate a provision for submitting representations online. The portal would also provide details of vacancies and the procedure for applying for transfers, he said.

According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be liable for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

Transfers during the non-transfer period, between June 1 and March 31, will be permitted only on administrative grounds, including promotions, disciplinary reasons, complaints, long leave arrangements and other administrative exigencies.

All transfers, including those sought by employees, during the transfer period will be processed through the online portal. The guidelines also provide for a maximum of three alternative station preferences in transfer applications.
The official said counselling for Executive Officers of town panchayats had already been conducted and postings issued based on it.

articles.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.
Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.
After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.
Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress.

“Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. Haldane and Laurie Baker. Gandhi, he said, derived his principles from all traditions and belief systems – Jainism, Vaishnavism, Christianity, and even communism. His attitude to gender, religion, or non-violence evolved through his engagements with various philosophies.

“I do not see him as a quintessentially Hindu thinker, quintessentially Indian thinker, [or] quintessentially traditional thinker. He transcends these lanes. Or Leftist, Rightist, Conservative; he is all three,” Dr. Guha added.

On the question of caste and the equations with the Ambedkarite principles, Dr. Guha said that Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper caste while Ambedkar was a dalit without emancipation and they could only take those paths. From the perspective of history and the future of India, the paths are converging. Asked if Gandhi’s methods are lost in the era of social media, he said the “cockroaches showed that they have it”. If the book came out a few months later, he said he would have added a few paragraphs on the Cockroach Janata Party movement.

articles.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges.
Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives.

The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors.

“No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore.

“We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu.

The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added.

While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. Santhosh, president of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Consumers Association.

In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges. These are not applicable because the court has stayed the green energy open access policy of the State, he added. More sub-stations and solutions for right of way challenges to lay lines on lands belonging to various government departments are among the other issues faced by investors that threaten to slow down solar energy projects.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme
Andhra Pradesh has received national recognition for its progress in controlling HIV, with six districts in the State achieving the ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 achieving the ‘Saksham’ status.

According to a release from the department, the districts of Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram achieved ‘Surakshit’ status, while the districts of Anakapalli, Anantapur, Bapatla, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, Kurnool, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam, Tirupati and YSR Kadapa achieved the ‘Saksham’ status.
The rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets, fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS(UNAIDS) as part of efforts to end the epidemic by 2030.

The three targets include ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 95% of those diagnosed; and achieving viral suppression in 95% of those receiving treatment.

According to the release, the percentage of people living with HIV who knew their status increased from 87.7% in April 2026 to 92.7% in October, and currently stands at 92.8%. Between April and October, 7,641 new HIV cases were identified through Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres.
The number of people receiving ART increased from 2,41,507 in April to 2,65,690 in October, an additional 24,183 patients. Viral suppression has been achieved in 96.4% of those undergoing treatment.
Reacting to the development, Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said 16 districts improved their performance between April and October.

The release stated that the A.P. State AIDS Control Society (APSACS) developed ‘Suraksha’ portal to monitor HIV testing, diagnosis and treatment services. It also launched ‘Each One Reach One’ initiative, to bring patients who had discontinued medication back into treatment. These two measures also helped the State achieve the targets.
Mr. Satya Kumar said priority was to ensure timely diagnosis, continuous treatment and quality healthcare without discrimination for everyone living with HIV.
APSACS Project Director Smaran Raj said the organisation was committed to bringing three more districts to ‘Surakshit’ status in the week.

articles.title: 14-year-old used AI chatbot to hack Agniveer ‘test’ website, wanted to earn money by selling it on dark web: Delhi police sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Haryana teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find a way into the test portal; preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed, Delhi Police sources say

A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh, who was apprehended for attempting to sell sensitive information linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web, used artificial intelligence tools to “identify data that could fetch him money and sought the chatbot’s help to hack into a website”, a senior official familiar with the investigation told The Hindu .
The boy gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in the Indian Armed Forces.

“Preliminary investigation has revealed that the boy managed to breach only the test website, gaining access to names and addresses. There is no indication so far that information relating to marks, ranks, results or other sensitive personnel records was compromised,” the official said.
During preliminary questioning, the boy told investigators that he was motivated by the prospect of making money.

“He said he first asked an AI chatbot to identify what kind of data could help him earn money. He then sought its assistance in finding a way to hack into the system and access such information,” the official said. The exact method used to gain access to the website is still being examined.

After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and advertised it on a dark web marketplace, claiming to possess personal records of around 4,000 Agniveer personnel and sought $500 for the purported database.

The Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile’s digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to establish its authenticity and determine the extent of the suspected breach.

The IFSO unit has also written to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), seeking clarification on the data available on the test website and the information accessed by the boy. The police are awaiting a response to ascertain precisely what information may have been compromised.

While the NIC provides digital infrastructure and hosts government portals, the ownership and maintenance of Agniveer personnel records rest with the Armed Forces and the concerned ministries, officials said.
As the accused is a juvenile, he was counselled and handed over to his parents. The police are consulting the Juvenile Justice Board on the further course of action.

articles.title: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year; there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001

The story so far: Within 23 days this year, three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal. Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026).

A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.

articles.title: FUJIFILM’s Spectrum tour enthrals visual creators, photography enthusiasts in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The three-day event featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture
A multi-city FUJIFILM India Spectrum Tour, bringing together of the brand’s entire range of imaging solutions from Instax cameras, digital cameras and lenses, concluded in Bengaluru recently.

The three-day event, held at the Venkatappa Art Gallery, featured specialised experience zones focusing on distinct creative mediums, including vlogging, cinematography, street photography and portraiture, attracted a large number of people.

Company executives highlighted the regional strategy behind selecting the city for this segment of the tour. "We are excited to connect with the city’s vibrant imaging community. Through Spectrum, we aim to bring our imaging heritage and cutting-edge technology closer to creators,"’ said Koji Wada, managing director of FUJIFILM India.

The tour was in Bengaluru after Gurugram and Ahmedabad, attracting local photography enthusiasts, visual creators and students who prefer to have a hands-on experience with FUJIFILM product ranges. A central component involved educational masterclasses led by established industry practitioners. Photographers including Sudhir Ramachandran and Prashant Godbole were among the participants.

Sessions covered architectural, landscape, and street photography. Other sessions led by technical experts covered niche genres such as astrophotography, wildlife documentation, and sports imaging. The event consolidated the company’s various product categories, including mirrorless camera systems, instant photography devices, and optical tools, under a unified interactive environment.

Arun Babu, associate director of the Imaging Solutions Division at FUJIFILM India, said, “In Bengaluru, through hands-on experiences, we encouraged visitors to experiment with our imaging solutions and discover new ways to express their creativity.”

articles.title: Kashmir’s famed saffron fields have been used as dumping grounds for three years: Mehbooba Mufti
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister says nearly 2,000 kanals of land have been damaged, threatening the livelihoods of 150 families; the NGT has directed a panel to inspect the site and recommend action

The committee will examine the extent of pollution caused by the waste dumping, assess its impact on saffron cultivation spread over approximately 2,000 kanals of land and adjoining areas, and ascertain whether the dumping site has obtained the requisite statutory clearances, officials said

articles.title: Immigration officers make arrest at Seattle airport in ‘distressing’ scene, delaying flight
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the affected family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would "engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred"

Masked immigration officers detained at least one person on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding, causing what the airline called a "distressing" scene for passengers and employees and delaying the Los Angeles-bound flight.

Video of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday (November 22, 2026) as a woman screams that her daughter is being taken and she has a work permit.
Online flight data showed that Alaska flight 1306, which had been scheduled to depart at 8:10 a.m., was delayed.
Alaska Airlines said Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

"We are concerned by this morning's law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306," the airline said. "We recognise how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests."
It added that the airline is committed to "treating every guest with dignity and respect".
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.
The arresting officers wore unmarked jackets and khaki pants. The video showed them struggling with someone on the ground as passengers surrounded by rolling suitcases looked on.
ICE has stepped up arrests at airports since the summer, especially targeting people who overstayed visas in the past.

Alaska Airlines said it was working with the Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, to see if protocols were followed, and also that it has raised concerns "directly with the appropriate authorities".

articles.title: South Korea Education Minister resigns amid AI cheating scandal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score
South Korea's Education Minister resigned on Sunday (November 22, 2026) over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted ahead of the country's key college entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday (November 15, 2026), when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial college entrance exam known as the Suneung.
The annual nine-hour Suneung is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country.

The confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures — including blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons but Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam.

"The exam concluded without any major incidents... However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance," Mr. Choi wrote on X.
"Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation," he added.
President Lee Jae Myung has accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday (November 16, 2026) whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied: "Due to my age, I am not confident I could."
Mr. Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday's (November 19, 2026) exam, where a vice minister instead announced the preventive measures.

Officials said 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during Thursday's (November 19, 2026) exam, nearly half of which were detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones that test takers had failed to hand over.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Leaders of the U.S., Russia and China agreed to begin talks on nuclear risk reduction but offered no details on institutionalising the dialogue process

While addressing the press after the November 19 summit with American and Chinese leaders in Shenzhen, the Chinese tech hub, Russian President Vladimir Putin responded to comparisons between the trilateral and the 1945 Yalta Conference . “What was wrong with Yalta? What was so bad about it?” he said, while responding to a question. “At Yalta, the victory over Nazism was codified... I wouldn’t mind — in fact, I would consider it right — to codify a victory over ‘neo-Nazism’ as well,” Mr. Putin said.

At the Yalta Conference, one of the most consequential diplomatic summits of the 20th century, Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, American President Franklin D. Roosevelt, and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill assembled in the Crimean city to discuss the post-war political order. In February 1945, when the summit was held, the Soviet Red Army had pushed deep into Eastern Europe and was marching towards Berlin while the Allied forces were advancing from Western Europe. The defeat of Nazi Germany was certain. The leaders decided that Germany would be divided, German militarism would be eliminated, and Nazi institutions would be dismantled. The summit played an important role in shaping the post-war European order.

In 1799, the British physician Francis Buchanan recorded that Muslims “long settled in Arakan” called themselves the “Rooinga”.

Many joined them, coming from Chittagong during colonial rule. articles.title: News in Frames | Living with the wounds of displacement

fullParagraphs: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya is significant, but refugees continue to face the threat of violence and restrictions on humanitarian access, as the situation in their homeland remains precarious

T he International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN’s top court, on November 19, ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during the military’s 2017 clearance operations in Rakhine State. This was the first time the world court held a country responsible for committing genocide.

The Rohingya, a predominantly Muslim ethnic minority, have faced decades of systematic discrimination in the Southeast Asian country, including the denial of citizenship, restrictions on movement and access to education, healthcare and livelihoods.

In August 2017, a military crackdown involving mass killings, sexual violence, and the burning of villages forced more than 7,40,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. They joined earlier waves of refugees who had escaped persecution. Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya now live in overcrowded camps in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar. Rohingya refugees in other countries such as India, Malaysia and Indonesia also face uncertain legal status, discrimination, detention and the threat of deportation.
Meanwhile, their homeland remains deeply troubled. Rakhine State has been engulfed in fighting between Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, a rebel group which now controls much of the region.

The Rohingya, many of whom remain internally displaced, face renewed insecurity, restrictions on humanitarian access and the threat of violence from competing armed forces. And for the refugees, a return to their homeland is neither desirable nor practical. While the ICJ verdict is significant and sets a strong precedent, it is unlikely to ease the suffering of the Rohingya.

Seeking safe harbour: The refugees being transported by a wooden boat to a temporary shelter in Krueng Raya, Aceh Besar, Indonesia, on April 8, 2013. The port has been a major landing point and temporary shelter site over the years.
Fleeing the inferno: Rohingya refugees flee as fires in Myanmar, allegedly started by the military, burn in the background, near Bangladesh in 2017.
Paddling into exile: Rohingya refugees cross the Naf River on an improvised raft to reach Bangladesh on November 12, 2017.
Longing for justice: Rohingya refugees watch the live announcement of the verdict in a genocide case against Myanmar on November 19, 2026
The agony of loss: Hamida, a Rohingya refugee, weeps as she holds her 40-day-old son, who died after their boat capsized before reaching the shore in Teknaf, Bangladesh, on September 14, 2017.

fullParagraphs: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia

The story so far: The battle for the most-sought-after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer. On November 16, the U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule (IFR) requiring companies to have licences to supply advanced American AI chips to data centre operators outside the U.S. with substantial computing power to businesses headquartered in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. The new rule restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry”. The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but Congress strengthened the extant legal framework only during the first Trump term when it passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It strengthened the U.S. government’s authority to control the movement of advanced technology originating in the country, and included curbing exports of sensitive technologies, including top-tier chips, with dual-use — both commercial and military — applications to countries such as China, Russia, and Iran.

A year later, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Chinese telecom equipment maker Huawei and its affiliates on the Entity List, effectively blocking their access to high-end semiconductors.

articles.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early
The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs.

A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her.

The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources.

Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early.

Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream.

“People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says.

A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics.
State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward.
“We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

articles.title: Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Requisition for appointment of 1,061 faculty posts for Engineering Colleges and 354 faculty posts for polytechnic colleges sent to BPSC

With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026).
“The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna.

These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative.
In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year.

The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS).

“The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27.

A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films.
Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference.

In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

articles.title: BJP’s invitation to Pakistan’s Minister vindicates Abdullah’s stance: J&K Deputy Chief Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan

J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that the BJP-led government’s move to invite Pakistan’s Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue Forum “vindicated the stand of National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah and vice president Omar Abdullah.”

Referring to the BJP’s stance after the 2025 Pahalgam attack, Mr. Choudhary said, “The BJP will say it will not talk to Pakistan. And when Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah advocate dialogue, the BJP will call them Pakistani. I want to ask the BJP: hasn’t a Pakistani Minister been invited to India on their invitation?”

He said the invitation to the Pakistani Minister proved that “the stance of my leaders was right then and is right now.” “The NC’s stance is the same as the one articulated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who would say, ‘You can choose your friends, but you cannot choose your neighbours.’ One must always maintain good relations with one’s neighbours,” said Mr. Choudhary.

Asking Pakistan to end terrorism, Mr. Choudhary said, “Both Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah have been asking Pakistan to end terrorism and close terror camps if Pakistan wants better relations. We stand behind our leaders.”
People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan.

“The two countries share a common history and several mutual concerns, including political issues, climate change, and water-related matters, which can only be addressed through engagement and dialogue. Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan

J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that the BJP-led government’s move to invite Pakistan’s Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue Forum “vindicated the stand of National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah and vice president Omar Abdullah.”

Referring to the BJP’s stance after the 2025 Pahalgam attack, Mr. Choudhary said, “The BJP will say it will not talk to Pakistan. And when Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah advocate dialogue, the BJP will call them Pakistani. I want to ask the BJP: hasn’t a Pakistani Minister been invited to India on their invitation?”

He said the invitation to the Pakistani Minister proved that “the stance of my leaders was right then and is right now.” “The NC’s stance is the same as the one articulated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who would say, ‘You can choose your friends, but you cannot choose your neighbours.’ One must always maintain good relations with one’s neighbours,” said Mr. Choudhary.

Asking Pakistan to end terrorism, Mr. Choudhary said, “Both Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah have been asking Pakistan to end terrorism and close terror camps if Pakistan wants better relations. We stand behind our leaders.”

People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan.

“The two countries share a common history and several mutual concerns, including political issues, climate change, and water-related matters, which can only be addressed through engagement and dialogue. Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

articles.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul launches a programme to provide dignified, alternative livelihoods to trans persons

The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness. Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.

“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood. We have decided that those among them who are interested will receive training from the police and be deployed at traffic signals. Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

She further added that another group of transgender persons would be trained to collect outstanding taxes, which could help address the staff shortage that leads to delayed collections and large pending amounts.

The Minister also added that each of these transgender individuals will be provided with training to engage in this work so that they can conduct better public interaction and do their work seamlessly. They will receive a stipend for the work, Ms. Paul said.

The West Bengal government has started an initiative to offer relief in paying outstanding property taxes, including in the actual sums and interest, to encourage defaulters to pay their outstanding balances.
According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.

In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment. A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community. The last census carried out in the state in 2011 put the number of transgender people in the state at 30,349. The actual number of people of the third gender may be higher, several groups working for the community say.

articles.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee

Supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) were allegedly attacked on Friday (November 20, 2026) by supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) outside a police station while party leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned by Kolkata Police at the Girish Park police station.

Videos of the scuffle and the assault on women supporters of the Trinamool were shared on social media and by the Mamata AITC. In the videos, groups of women alleged to be BJP supporters were seen chasing another group of women. Supporters of the Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee. The BJP leaders denied allegations of the assault but claimed that Trinamool supporters were trying to incite tensions by gathering outside the police station.

“@BJP4Bengal workers gathered outside Girish Park Police Station today, seemingly intent on harassing, heckling and assaulting our workers, did not even spare ordinary citizens and parents who had come to pick up their children from school,” the party shared on social media. The Mamata AITC leader raised questions on the role of politics.

The police complaint against the Diamond Harbour MP was filed in connection with remarks reportedly made by him on 29 October, in which he criticised sections of the police administration, alleging that officers were acting under political pressure. Mr. Banerjee took to social media to share videos of BJP leaders, including Suvendu Adhikari, alleging threats to the police when they were in the Opposition.

After the BJP came to power, several FIRs were registered against Abhishek Banerjee. He has been summoned to appear before the police on numerous occasions. Later in the day, the Trinamool leader filed a Zero FIR at Girish Park Police Station, highlighting how Suvendu Adhikari, Dilip Ghosh, and other BJP leaders threatened the Kolkata Police and the West Bengal Police on multiple occasions.

“The expertise and urgency shown by Girish Park PS in connection with Abhishek Banerjee’s matter—we hope the same expertise and urgency will be shown by them in connection with this Zero FIR, and that they will investigate the matter,” Arka Nag, an advocate representing Trinamool Congress leader, said.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 21 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Odisha Chief Minister said heavy rainfall was expected in Mayurbhanj and Balasore over the next 24 hours, with its impact likely to extend to neighbouring Jajpur, Bhadrak, Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur districts
As many as 14 flights were cancelled at the Birsa Munda Airport in Ranchi on Saturday (November 21) due to inclement weather triggered by cyclone ‘Akvan’, an official said.
Cyclone Akvan causes 14 Ranchi airport flight cancellations due to poor visibility and bad weather.

Relief operations are underway on a war footing in Odisha’s Ganjam district after Cyclone Akvan. An ODRAF team carried out a tree-cutting operation under the Jarau Nal bridge in Chhandikendu village to clear the affected area.
Normalcy has been restored at Puri beach after Cyclone Akvan. Beach activities have resumed, bringing the shoreline back to life after the disruption caused by the cyclone.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu sought central assistance of nearly ₹100 crore for the restoration of horticultural crops damaged by cyclones Arnab and Murasu.

“Naidu has written a letter to Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Shivraj Singh Chouhan, seeking additional financial assistance for the restoration of horticulture crops damaged by two consecutive cyclones,” a press release said.
The cyclones damaged crops across 29,960 hectares in 18 districts, affecting 71,576 farmers and causing losses estimated at ₹1,092 crore, he said.

The cyclone had considerably lost its intensity when it made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha. “The cyclonic storm Akvan crossed the south coastal Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh close to Gopalpur with a wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph during 7.30 a.m. to 8.30 a.m.,” said the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Landfall of Cyclone Akvan nears Odisha and Andhra Pradesh coasts as land interaction begins, with heavy rainfall and prolonged impact anticipated.
The depression is likely to move nearly northwards over Odisha and weaken further into a low-pressure area during next 6 hours, said IMD

articles.title: Group of minors assault man, woman at Kurla garden; eight detained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The attack took place at Pramod Mahajan Garden behind a mall in Kurla West, a police official said

A group of minors allegedly assaulted a young man and a woman at a public garden in the eastern suburb of Kurla, Mumbai, with a video of the incident going viral on social media, police said on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
The attack took place at Pramod Mahajan Garden behind a mall in Kurla West, an official said.

The clip, which surfaced on social media on Friday (November 20, 2026), showed the young man and woman being surrounded by a group of minors, some appearing to be as young as 10 years old, who then proceeded to hit them with a stick, punch and kick them, before chasing after them as they tried to escape.

Taking serious cognisance of the viral footage, police identified the minors involved in the assault and registered a case under section 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and other relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the official said.
Eight minors have been detained and will be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB), he added.

articles.title: Break free of limiting beliefs to achieve new heights: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Narendra Modi joins Platinum Jubilee celebrations of the first IIT of the country and says the institute has and will continue to play a major role in nation building

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 21, 2026) said that if people go ahead with the “nation first” mindset, then new opportunities will come their way. He asked students to break free of limiting beliefs to achieve new heights, at the Platinum jubilee celebrations of the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.

“This place has always come forward in building the nation at every stage of the country since its independence,” Mr. Modi said while addressing the students at the 75th anniversary celebrations at IIT Kharagpur, which is also the first IIT of independent India. He also hoped that the institute will continue to make similar contributions in building the future of the nation.

“We have limiting beliefs; we limit our thoughts, our dreams, our aspirations, our talent, and give up. But we only reach our full potential if we break free of the limits to unlock new possibilities,” Mr. Modi said. He added that people put limit to their own thoughts, restricting the opportunities in their lives and of the nation.
Mr Modi said that during his tenure as the PM, he has broken the limits and achieved many such goals which people believed to be “impossible”.

“ Poverty in India was known to be a permanent problem. But there was no real change made through policy; they only made files. People took the situation for granted. But when we came to power, we changed this mentality and empowered the poor and started schemes to get them out of poverty,” Mr. Modi said. He added that according to a World Bank report, in the last 12-13 years at least 50 crore people in India have been taken out of poverty.

Mr. Modi added that in the coming days, when India is going forward towards a “Viksit Bharat”, IIT Kharagpur is sure to play a major role in building that dream. The PM further said that he hopes the 100 years of IIT Kharagpur will be celebrated in the Vikshit Bharat in the coming years.

VIDEO | Kharagpur, West Bengal: At the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur, Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, "Break the limit, unlock the possibilities. Let me share a few examples with you today. Just think, until 20 years ago, poverty was considered a permanent problem in our country. Five decades ago, slogans were raised from the Red Fort about eradicating poverty. However, whenever it came to taking action at the policy level, the entire system would simply prepare files and sit idle." (Source: Narendra Modi YT) (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)
West Bengal Governor R.N. Ravi , Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay were among the others present at the 75-year program.

Meanwhile, the director of the institute took the stage and said that under the PM’s leadership, they are now remaining true to the mission of IIT Kharagpur. “From grassroots to skyrockets, that is the new IIT Kharagpur,” Professor Suman Chakraborty said. He also added that IIT Kharagpur alumni and Google CEO Sundar Pichai have offered a 5 million dollar support for applied Artificial Intelligence research.

fullParagraphs: Ravi Hanj was detained during security checks while attempting to travel abroad, say Kerala Police sources. He will be handed over to Karnataka Police

Kannada writer Ravi Hanj, who is at the centre of a major controversy over alleged derogatory remarks against 12th-century social reformer Basavanna in his book Basava Mantapa and in interviews around the book , has been detained by Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel at Cochin International Airport in Keralam.

Mr. Hanj was detained during security checks on Saturday (November 21, 2026) while attempting to travel abroad, State police sources said. He was being taken for medical examinations, the sources said.
The CISF took Mr. Hanj into custody acting on a lookout notice issued against him by the Belagavi police. He will be handed over to the Karnataka Police, sources added.
Mr. Hanj was recently booked by the police in Bengaluru, Belagavi, Bagewadi and Vijayapura following complaints alleged derogatory remarks against Basavanna and the Lingayat community.

The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday decided to confiscate his book following complaints by Veerashiva-Lingayat groups. The book’s publisher, Vishweshwar Bhat, has also been named in the Bengaluru and Vijayapura FIRs. The book is a compilation of columns published in the Viswavani newspaper under the same title Basava Mantapa . It was released as a book in Bengaluru on November 15.

The government decided to confiscate the book following representations from Basava Samiti that alleged that the writer made the derogatory remarks in the book and in an interview published on Viswavani’s social media channels on November 13. The complaints have sought legal action against the writer, editor and others allegedly involved, and requested authorities to prevent further circulation of the book and content that could hurt religious sentiments. The BJP also demanded action against the writer.

Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, briefing the media after Thursday’s Cabinet meeting, had said they were not banning the book but “forfeiting all copies”, and there was a provision for the same under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. However, there had been no notification from the government till November 21 afternoon to empower the police to forfeit the books.

articles.title: People will never forget BRS corruption: Telangana Congress president Mahesh Kumar Goud

fullParagraphs: Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president and MLC Mahesh Kumar Goud claimed that people would never forget the alleged misappropriation of public money by the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) government and resources given the large-scale corruption during its decade-long rule.

Speaking to the media in Nizamabad, he said several instances of corruption during the previous regime had come to light with evidence, and those responsible could not escape accountability. His response comes in the wake of BRS party’s relentless criticism of corruption charges against the Congress government.

He alleged that former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekhar Rao and former Minister T. Harish Rao were responsible for the alleged exploitation of Telangana’s water resources during the BRS regime. The Kaleshwaram project, conceived as a major irrigation initiative, had resulted in the wastage of public money worth several lakh crore rupees, he charged.

The BRS regime had also witnessed large-scale irregularities in land transactions and land-related matters, he alleged, adding that the list of alleged corruption cases under the previous government was extensive.
To a question, Mr. Goud described Congress leader Rahul Gandhi as a leader committed to serving the country, and that national service and public welfare remained his priorities.

On inter-State water disputes, he asserted that Telangana would not surrender even a single drop of its legitimate share of water. The Congress government was committed to protecting the State’s interests and ensuring that its rightful water allocations were secured, he said.
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy was governing with determination, keeping development as the government’s principal objective, the TPCC president said.
